title: A Motor Neuron Is a Combination

scenes.tts: Where does a motor neuron come from? In the neural tube, Sonic hedgehog sets up a gradient. Progenitors read their position in it, and one stripe, called p M N, makes motor neurons. Yet a progenitor there does not contain a gene for motor neuron. It contains three or four transcription factors. None is specific to motor neurons on its own. A motor neuron is what that particular set spells.

scenes.visual: Neural tube with stacked stripes and a Shh gradient; the pMN stripe lights up; zoom to one cell where a crossed-out 'motor neuron gene?' box is replaced by four factor chips that together spell 'motor neuron'.
scenes.narration: Where does a motor neuron come from? In the neural tube, Sonic hedgehog sets up a gradient. Progenitors read their position in it, and one stripe, called pMN, makes motor neurons. scenes.tts: Around its final division, a motor neuron turns on a new set. These are Islet one or its relative Islet two, L H X three, and M N X one. They are the markers you stain for to find a motor neuron. But L H X three is also made in a neighbour of the motor neuron, the V two interneuron. One protein sits in two different cell types.
scenes.caption: Around its final division, a motor neuron turns on a new set. These are Isl1 or its relative Isl2, Lhx3, and Mnx1. They are the markers you stain for to find a motor neuron. But Lhx3 is also made in a neighbour of the motor neuron, the V2 interneuron. One protein sits in two different cell types.
scenes.visual: A motor-neuron cell gains three chips (Isl1 with 'or Isl2', Lhx3, Mnx1); stain rings light them; a V2 interneuron cell appears beside it holding the same blue Lhx3 chip.
scenes.narration: Around its final division, a motor neuron turns on a new set. These are Isl1 or its relative Isl2, Lhx3, and Mnx1. They are the markers you stain for to find a motor neuron. But Lhx3 is also made in a neighbour of the motor neuron, the V2 interneuron. One protein sits in two different cell types.

scenes.tts: Now try an experiment in the chick neural tube. Put L H X three into cells that have no Islet one. You get V two interneuron genes. The reason is a partner. L H X three binds a cofactor called N L I directly. That complex triggers V two differentiation.
scenes.caption: Now try an experiment in the chick neural tube. Put Lhx3 into cells that have no Isl1. You get V2 interneuron genes. The reason is a partner. Lhx3 binds a cofactor called NLI directly. That complex triggers V2 differentiation.
scenes.visual: Lhx3 drawn as a cup with a socket; Isl1 slot is empty and crossed; the NLI plug snaps into the socket and an arrow leads to 'V2 interneuron genes'.
scenes.narration: Now try an experiment in the chick neural tube. Put Lhx3 into cells that have no Isl1. You get V2 interneuron genes. The reason is a partner. Lhx3 binds a cofactor called NLI directly. That complex triggers V2 differentiation.

scenes.tts: Add Islet one to the same cell, and the result changes. Islet one competes for N L I. It displaces L H X three onto a high-affinity site in the C terminal region of Islet one. The complex that forms then promotes motor neuron genes.
scenes.caption: Add Isl1 to the same cell, and the result changes. Isl1 competes for NLI. It displaces Lhx3 onto a high-affinity site in the C-terminal region of Isl1. The complex that forms then promotes motor neuron genes.
scenes.visual: Same cell: the old V2 result clears; Isl1 arrives and takes NLI from the Lhx3 socket, NLI stays bound under Isl1; Isl1's C-terminal tail then plugs into the Lhx3 socket; a green 'motor neuron genes' chip appears.
scenes.narration: Add Isl1 to the same cell, and the result changes. Isl1 competes for NLI. It displaces Lhx3 onto a high-affinity site in the C-terminal region of Isl1. The complex that forms then promotes motor neuron genes.

scenes.tts: So the cell is not reading a gene that says motor neuron. It is reading which assembly wins a competition for a shared partner. The competition is a contest for one binding site. Look at the same surface of L H X three. It holds N L I in one complex. In the other, it holds a segment of Islet one.

scenes.visual: The two complexes side by side with their outcomes, NLI bound in both; rings pulse on the same Lhx3 socket in both, then labels 'holds NLI' and 'holds a segment of Isl1' appear.
scenes.narration: So the cell is not reading a gene that says motor neuron. It is reading which assembly wins a competition for a shared partner. The competition is a contest for one binding site. Look at the same surface of Lhx3. It holds NLI in one complex. In the other, it holds a segment of Isl1.

scenes.tts: Two tests, two questions. Put Islet one and L H X three together into one chick cell, and motor neuron genes come up. Delete Islet one in the mouse, and motor neurons are not generated at all. Adding a factor shows what it can impose. Deleting it shows what cannot be built without it. Keep this rule. A motor neuron is spelled by a combination of factors, not by one master gene.

scenes.visual: Two rows: chick, Isl1 plus Lhx3 gives green motor neuron genes; mouse, crossed-out Isl1 gives no motor neurons. Rows fade to the rule.
